packageRules.description: Never merge a major on its own. A major is a reading job, and the dashboard is where it waits.

Payload is one product across six packages and they must move together; a mismatch does not build. Manual because a Payload minor can carry a schema change, which needs a migration rather than a merge.
React and its types move together or the build disagrees with itself.
The Tailwind package and its postcss plugin are versioned in step.
Next is read by hand. This project pins it, the framework's own agent notes warn that its APIs move, and a bump here can change how every page is rendered.
The toolchain cannot change what a visitor sees, only whether the gate is honest about it, and the gate runs on the same pull request. Patch and minor merge themselves once CI is green.
Runtime dependencies merge themselves on a patch only, and only behind the render comparison, which fails a bot's pull request if a single element on any page moved.
Sharp compiles native binaries per platform and the build machine is not this laptop. Read it.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A security fix does not wait for Monday.
